content.text: Triage is above; I'm asking you to pick how four of the product fixes should work.

questions.question: #231 ("needs your decision" / "add a merchant" shows 201 items and asks about a person you know): how should Moneo handle transactions with no clear merchant?

options.label: Auto-fill, never ask (Recommended)
options.description: Code reads the counterparty name and the AI organizer labels the rest (marked AI, undoable). Drop the 'add a merchant' prompt; only real conflicts like possible duplicates stay in 'needs decision'.

options.label: Auto-fill, ask on low confidence
options.description: Same, but low-confidence guesses still go to a much shorter review list.

options.label: Hide the prompt only
options.description: Keep the current data and just stop showing the merchant prompt and the count.

questions.question: #230 (categorizing transactions in review): which changes do you want?

options.label: Bulk 'apply to all' (Recommended)
options.description: One button that sets a category for every row in a group, or skips the whole step.

options.label: Show everything in one pass (Recommended)
options.description: Load every pending item up front so you don't close it and find more waiting.

options.label: Edit after deciding (Recommended)
options.description: Change a category you already gave, from the review list and from the transaction.

questions.question: #229 (old bank account that isn't connected): after you say 'yes, this is mine' once, what should happen?

options.label: Remember as own untracked account (Recommended)
options.description: Save that IBAN/name as your own untracked account in Accounts, mark every matching transaction (past and future) as an own transfer, and stop asking.

options.label: Create a tracked manual account
options.description: Add it as a full manual account with a balance you keep up to date.

options.label: Offer both on the first yes
options.description: Ask once: track it, or just mark it as yours.

input.title: #230 categorize review
input.task:
Fix GitHub issue #230 in Moneo: the review flow for categorizing transactions. The owner wants all three:
1. **Bulk "apply to all"**: one action to set one category for every row in a group (or for all remaining rows), and a way to skip the step entirely, for an owner who doesn't want to categorize one by one.
2. **One pass**: show every pending item up front. Today the owner finishes, closes it, and finds more feedback waiting, again and again. Find out why items appear in batches (pagination, a background job adding more, a limit) and fix the cause so the owner sees everything in one go.
3. **Edit after deciding**: a category already given can be changed again, from the review list and from the transaction.
Owner category choices are owner corrections. Keep history and undo (AGENTS.md). Note: a sibling agent is working on #231 (removing the "add a merchant" prompt), so stay focused on categories and avoid touching merchant-prompt code.

input.title: #229 old own account
input.task:
Fix GitHub issue #229 in Moneo: the owner has an old bank account that isn't connected. Moneo asked "is this you?" about a transfer to it, and the owner said yes, but then it asked again for each of the other 8–10 transactions with the same account.

Owner's decision: **Remember it as an own untracked account.** On the first "yes, this is mine", save that identifier (IBAN/name) as one of the owner's own untracked accounts (it shows in the Accounts page under accounts Moneo doesn't track), mark every matching transaction, past and future (imports and bank sync), as an own transfer, and never ask about that account again. Look at lib/finance/own-transfers.ts, the own-account proposal card (components/iou-card.tsx "Own account proposal"), the transaction drawer's "my own account Moneo doesn't track" option, and the home/overview prompt. Fix the class: the confirmation must apply to the identifier, not to one transaction. Keep undo: undoing the confirmation reverts all the transactions it reclassified. Check chat/voice paths that create the same proposal.

Agreed with the user on 2026-10-29/30 for the voice feature (built on [[voice-feature-branch-workflow]]):
- Calls: OpenAI GPT-Live (`gpt-live-1`, $0.05/min) with client delegation. GPT-Live talks; every real request goes to the existing `/api/chat` Moneo agent (user's chat model, GPT-6 Luna) in the same conversation. WebRTC set up server-side via `@ai-sdk/openai` live support, so the key never reaches the browser.
- While Moneo works, it says what it's doing out loud ("let me look through your transactions"), not only on screen.
- Several tasks at once: each request is its own parallel task, with **no limit**. Results are spoken as they arrive, held while the user is mid-sentence. Corrections (decided 2026-10-30): if the old task can still stop (only reading, no card made yet), stop it and start the new one. If it already made a card, let it finish, then run the corrected task, and auto-dismiss the old card with a "replaced" note. App code decides this, not the model. Each task also has an ✕ to stop it.
- Call personality: casual friend (short, warm, occasional "mm-hm"). Language: follow the user (English, German, mixed). Voice: Claude picks a natural default, plus a Settings voice picker with "Play sample".
- Confirm is tap-only on cards (tray during the call, and Overview "Waiting for you"). Voice never accepts.
- Mic: one button, same for tap or hold, with live words. At the end you choose **Send** (goes now; you can close the app) or **Done** (edit in the box). A voice note is just a spoken message, not a separate feature.
- Chat and artifact runs must keep going after the app is closed (Next `after()`, cancel only explicitly).
- After a call: summary card plus collapsible transcript in the chat. Both phone and desktop matter. No cost limits for now.
- Later items are in BACKLOG.md "Voice: later" (ElevenLabs, separate speech-to-text and text-to-speech pipeline, discreet mode, etc.).

**Why:** the user wants the coolest real voice agent, but with financial truth staying in app code.
**How to apply:** build steps against these decisions; ask before changing any of them.

## #227 plan: choose your speech-to-text (chat mic only, not calls)

**What the owner sees.** Settings → Voice gets a new **Speech to text** section:
- **Engine:** OpenAI (today's live words) · **On this computer** (a local model) · **OpenRouter** (an audio-capable model).
- **On this computer:** a short list of models Moneo suggests, each with its size, languages and speed:
  - Moonshine Base, ~60 MB, English only, very fast
  - Whisper Base, ~150 MB, multilingual incl. German, fast
  - Whisper Small, ~500 MB, multilingual, best quality, slower
  - Distil-Whisper, English, a good balance

  The owner gets the model and then **points Moneo at it**. On desktop that's a native "Choose model…" file dialog. On the source install it's a path field, because a browser can't hand over a file path. Below that sits a **Try it** button: say a sentence and see the text.
- **OpenRouter:** a model dropdown filtered to models that accept audio input, using your existing OpenRouter key.
- The mic button doesn't change. The chosen engine shows as a small label while recording.

**How it works**
1. The browser records the same way it does now and sends the audio to Moneo's own server (`/api/voice/transcribe`) on 127.0.0.1. The phone over Tailscale works too, because the model runs on the computer, not the phone.
2. The server picks the engine from Settings:
   - **Local:** runs the model in a background worker, so the app stays responsive. It loads on the first use and unloads after it sits idle for a while. Merchant and people names from `voice-vocabulary.ts` go in as a hint, so names come out right. Audio never leaves the machine.
   - **OpenRouter:** sends the recording to the chosen model and asks for a plain transcript.
   - **OpenAI:** today's live path, unchanged.
3. **Fallback (your choice):** if the chosen engine is missing or fails and an OpenAI key exists, Moneo uses OpenAI and shows a small note, "Used OpenAI, local model unavailable". With no key, the mic shows why it can't work.
4. **Live words:** local and OpenRouter transcribe after you stop (the Send/Done flow stays the same). Optionally, the local engine re-transcribes every 1–2 s while you talk, so words still appear as you speak.

**Building blocks**
- `lib/ai/speech/`: one `transcribe(audio, hints)` contract per engine, the engine choice and the fallback rule, all unit-tested with fake engines (pure lib, no mocks of the app).
- Runtime for local models: **transformers.js + onnxruntime-node** (prebuilt for Windows, macOS and Linux, a plain npm dependency, nothing extra to install for source users). Desktop adds it to the packaged native modules. The alternative is whisper.cpp (a single `.bin` file, very fast), but it has no prebuilt Linux/macOS server binaries, so we'd have to build and ship it ourselves.
- Settings stored like the other preferences. The model path is a machine-local setting. Reset all data clears the choice but never deletes the model file.
- README: how to download a suggested model and point Moneo at it.

**PRs (in order)**
1. Engine contract + Settings section + OpenAI behind it + fallback. No visible change for current owners. *(Sonnet)*
2. Local model engine: worker, model picker, suggested list, Try it, desktop packaging, README. *(Opus: native module packaging on 4 platforms)*
3. OpenRouter audio engine. *(Sonnet)*
4. Optional: live words for the local engine. *(Sonnet)*

input.task:
Moneo issue #227 (configurable speech-to-text for the CHAT MIC only; voice calls/GPT-Live stay untouched). You build **PR 1 of 4**: the engine contract, the Settings section and the fallback. No local model and no OpenRouter yet. Later PRs add those on top of yours, so make the contract clean.

Today the chat mic (lib/ai/use-voice-input.ts, lib/ai/voice-recorder.ts) streams PCM to OpenAI realtime transcription through app/api/voice/session/route.ts (gpt-live-transcribe, vocabulary hints from lib/ai/voice-vocabulary.ts) and shows live words.

Build:
1. `lib/ai/speech/` with one engine contract. Batch engines take recorded audio plus hints and return text. The existing OpenAI live path becomes the `openai` engine with unchanged behaviour. Add the engine choice and the fallback rule as a pure, unit-tested function: if the chosen engine is unavailable or fails and an OpenAI key exists, use OpenAI and report that a fallback happened. If there's no key, return a clear reason the mic can't work.
2. A server route (e.g. `app/api/voice/transcribe/route.ts`) that batch engines will use. It accepts recorded audio from the browser (PCM16 or WAV, size-limited, validated with Zod) and calls the chosen engine, owner auth like the other voice routes. With only OpenAI today it can call OpenAI's batch transcription (/v1/audio/transcriptions) for a non-live mode, or simply be wired with a registry ready for engines; pick the smaller one that still exercises the contract.
3. Client: the recorder keeps live streaming when the engine is `openai`. For batch engines it captures audio and posts it on Send/Done. Show a small note in the mic UI when a fallback was used. The Send/Done UX doesn't change.
4. Settings → Voice: a "Speech to text" section with the engine choice (today only OpenAI is selectable; leave room for "On this computer" and "OpenRouter"), stored like the other owner preferences (see lib/settings.ts and its test about unreadable stored preferences). Reset all data clears it.
5. Tests: engine selection and fallback (fake engines), route validation and auth, audio encoding. No real API calls.
Agreed design for the later PRs, for context only, don't build it: local models via transformers.js + onnxruntime-node in a worker, with suggested models (Moonshine Base, Whisper Base/Small, Distil-Whisper), a Download button and Choose file; an OpenRouter audio-input model engine; live words for local as a stacked PR.

## Rules for every child
- Repo: Moneo (indkhan/Moneo). Read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly (no comments in code, surgical changes, tests only for real behaviour, hit every surface, desktop + source install both work).
- Read the full GitHub issue first: `gh issue view 227 --comments`. Recheck the current tree before changing anything.
- Work only in your own worktree. Branch `t3/issue-227-speech-engines` from current `origin/main` (`git fetch origin && git switch -c <branch> origin/main`). Commit each step in plain language, ending each commit message with:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- Other agents work in parallel against the SAME shared moneo-qa test backend and QA app port 3100: never run `npm run qa:reset`, never `docker compose -p moneo-qa down`, never touch the owner's backend (.env, port 3000, Docker project `moneo`). If port 3100 is serving another checkout, wait and retry; never kill a process you didn't start.
- Mock AI providers; no real paid calls.
- Before finishing: `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`; verify-ui skill for the Settings change (light/dark/mobile) with evidence in the PR.
- Push, open a PR to `main` with `gh pr create`. Body: what changed and why, "Part 1 of #227" (don't close the issue), how it was verified. End the PR body with:
  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
  Never merge.
- If something is ambiguous, choose what best fits AGENTS.md and note it in the PR.
- Final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

input.title: #152 Wealth charts and news
input.task:
Build Moneo issue #152: per-position price charts and news on the Wealth page for Scalable Capital positions.

The owner's decision: **the chart comes from the last sync and news loads live on open.**
- Tapping a Scalable position on Wealth opens a detail view (a drawer or page, matching how the app does transaction details) with a price chart. Periods: 1D/1W/1M/1Y/Max, whichever Scalable's `get_security_chart` timeframes support. Mark the owner's own buys and sells on the chart from the stored trade history (lib/scalable/history.ts and history-job.ts already read charts and trade details; reuse them).
- Store the chart points during the regular Scalable sync (lib/scalable/sync.ts) so the chart works offline and costs no extra calls on open. Add a new ordered migration in supabase/migrations/ and keep lib/schema.ts aligned. It must work on the desktop's bundled Postgres. Prices are decimal text or integer minor units with an explicit currency, never floats for money. Show "as of <sync time>".
- News: fetched live from `get_security_news` when the detail opens, with a loading state and a clear offline/error state. Never block the chart on it.
- Read-only. No trading changes. Scalable writes stay card-only.
- Hit every surface: the mobile layout, light and dark, and a chat tool or artifact if there's an obvious existing read-tools spot (lib/scalable/read-tools.ts) for "show me the chart for X". Make sure disconnecting Scalable and reset all data remove the stored chart data.
- Mock Scalable in tests. On the QA app use a mocked or stand-in connection. Never call the real account.

## Rules
- Read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly. Read `gh issue view 152 --comments`.
- Work only in your own worktree, on branch `t3/issue-152-wealth-charts` from current `origin/main` (`git fetch origin && git switch -c <branch> origin/main`). Commit each step in plain language, ending each message with:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- The moneo-qa backend and QA port 3100 are shared with other agents: never `npm run qa:reset`, never `docker compose -p moneo-qa down`, never touch the owner's backend (.env, port 3000, project `moneo`). If 3100 is busy with another checkout, wait and retry; never kill a process you didn't start.
- Before finishing: `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:db`; verify-ui skill (light/dark/mobile) with the evidence in the PR.
- Push and open a PR to `main` (`Closes #152`), ending the body with:
  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
  Never merge.
- Final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

One "yes" on an own-account card now remembers that account. It marks every matching transaction, past and future, as an own transfer and doesn't ask again.

- **What it saves:** the account goes on the Accounts page under the accounts Moneo doesn't track. It's saved by IBAN, or by the name on the payment when the bank gave no IBAN.
- **What it marks:** imports and bank sync mark later payments automatically. A name match also needs the name in the payment text and no other IBAN on the row, so a refund that only carries your name is left alone. The other open "your own account?" cards for the same account are closed.
- **Undo:** undoing any one of those transfers in the transaction drawer reverts all the transactions the confirmation reclassified and forgets the account. Accounts you add by hand still undo one transaction at a time.
- **Chat and voice:** both use the same path as the card, so they behave the same.
- **Migration:** `202611160001_confirmed_own_accounts.sql` makes the IBAN optional and adds a name key and a "confirmed" flag. It uses no extensions, so it runs on the desktop app's Postgres.

**Verification:**
- Two new database tests (`lib/finance/own-transfers.live.test.ts`, run by `npm run test:db`) pass: one yes marks all, closes the other card and marks a later import, and one undo reverts all. The IBAN-less name case passes too.
- `lib/schema.live.test.ts`, lint and `tsc` are clean on my files.
- I applied the migration to the shared `moneo-qa` database for the tests and removed it afterwards. The test data is gone too.
- `npm test` has five failing files. Two need the `unpdf` package, which is missing from the `node_modules` I borrowed because `npm ci` kept stalling. The other three timed out under load and pass when run alone.

**Not done:**
- No light/dark/mobile screenshots and no `npm run build`. The only visible changes are one line of card text and a "matched by name" label in the Accounts list.
- Undoing a single transfer of a hand-added account still leaves that account saved, so the next import marks it again. That is the same as before.

## Why the tests timed out
In the full suite, `lib/cron.test.ts` and four heavy page tests timed out at 5 s. Run alone, they passed. Two causes:

#233 is up as [PR #253](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/253), and I'll merge it once CI is green. It does three things:

- **Workflow builder:** it does the same when it bundles background jobs.

Fix GitHub issue #237 in Moneo: make failures outside workflows observable, and enforce async handling.

1. Recount the empty catches and ignored promises in lib/, server actions and route handlers.
2. For each one, decide who owns the failure, then do one of three things: return an actionable failure, persist a job outcome, or route it to a named existing handler.
3. Add type-aware lint (no-floating-promises, no-misused-promises, switch-exhaustiveness-check) for lib/, workflows/ and server actions. Introduce it incrementally and keep lint time reasonable.
4. Don't add generic retries or catch-and-log wrappers, and never log financial data or credentials.
5. Add a row to the AGENTS.md rules table for the new enforcement.

If the full scope is too big for one reviewable PR, deliver the lint plus the fixes for lib/, and list the rest in the PR body.

Moneo issue #227 (configurable speech-to-text for the CHAT MIC only; voice calls/GPT-Live untouched). You build **PR 1 of 4**: the engine contract, the Settings section and the fallback. No local model or OpenRouter yet; later PRs add those on top, so keep the contract clean.

Today the chat mic (lib/ai/use-voice-input.ts, lib/ai/voice-recorder.ts) streams PCM to OpenAI realtime transcription through app/api/voice/session/route.ts. That route uses gpt-live-transcribe with vocabulary hints from lib/ai/voice-vocabulary.ts, and the mic shows live words.

Build:
1. **Engine contract.** Create `lib/ai/speech/` with one engine contract: batch engines take the recorded audio plus hints and return text. The existing OpenAI live path becomes the `openai` engine, with unchanged behaviour. Add engine choice and fallback as a pure, unit-tested function:
   - If the chosen engine is unavailable or fails and an OpenAI key exists, use OpenAI and report that a fallback happened.
   - If there's no key, return a clear reason the mic can't work.
2. **Batch route.** A server route for batch engines (e.g. `app/api/voice/transcribe/route.ts`). It accepts recorded audio (PCM16 or WAV, size-limited, validated with Zod) and calls the chosen engine, with owner auth like the other voice routes. Wire it to an engine registry. If it's small, add OpenAI batch transcription (/v1/audio/transcriptions) as a second mode; otherwise the registry alone is enough.
3. **Client.** Keep live streaming for `openai`. For batch engines, capture the audio and post it on Send/Done. Show a small note in the mic UI when the fallback was used. The Send/Done UX doesn't change.
4. **Settings.** Add a "Speech to text" section under Settings → Voice with the engine choice. Today only OpenAI is selectable; leave room for "On this computer" and "OpenRouter". Store it like the other owner preferences (see lib/settings.ts and its unreadable-preference test). Reset all data clears it.
5. **Tests.** Engine selection and fallback (fake engines), route validation and auth, audio encoding. No real API calls.

Home is built for one currency (the workspace display currency) for now.

=== #161
Add German as an interface language, chosen in Settings.

A first pass was started in a worktree and discarded; this is what it did, as a starting point:

- `lib/settings.ts`: `locale` becomes `z.enum(["en-GB", "de-DE"])` (default `en-GB`) and doubles as the language preference.

- `app/layout.tsx`: set `<html lang>` to `de` or `en` from the workspace locale.
- `app/api/chat/route.ts` and `app/api/artifacts/route.ts`: tell the model to answer and write artifacts in German when the locale is `de-DE`, keeping names and quoted user text as given.
- `app/settings/actions.test.ts`: test that saving `de-DE` persists the locale.

Still open:

- Translating the UI strings (pages, home widgets, command palette, errors). The first pass only switched the AI's language.

Parent tracker: #224. Split out of #235.

Several applied migrations (reservation and reviewed-balance functions, wealth and goal date checks, budget rollover, bank observations, loan repayments) fall back to `'Europe/Berlin'` when a workspace has no `workspace_settings` row, and `workspace_settings.timezone` and `spending_plans.rollover_from` default to Berlin in the schema.

The app now saves the detected device time zone on the first workspace load (`requireWorkspace`), so the fallback is only reachable for a workspace that has not been loaded by the app yet.

input.task:
Build Moneo issue #152: per-position price charts and news on the Wealth page for Scalable Capital positions.

The owner decided: **the chart comes from the last sync, and news loads live when the detail opens.**

**Detail view**
- Tapping a Scalable position on Wealth opens a detail view with a price chart. Use a drawer or page, whichever matches how the app shows transaction details.
- Offer the periods 1D/1W/1M/1Y/Max, as far as Scalable's `get_security_chart` timeframes allow.
- Mark the owner's own buys and sells on the chart from the stored trade history. lib/scalable/history.ts and history-job.ts already read charts and trade details, so reuse them.

**Storing the chart**
- Store the chart points during the regular Scalable sync (lib/scalable/sync.ts), so the chart works offline and opening it costs no extra calls.
- Add a new ordered migration with a unique timestamp prefix later than `202611160041`. Keep lib/schema.ts aligned. It must work on the desktop's bundled Postgres.
- Prices are decimal text or integer minor units with an explicit currency, never floats for money. Use the formatter in lib/finance/format.ts.
- Show "as of <sync time>".

**News**
- Fetch it live from `get_security_news` when the detail opens, with a loading state and a clear offline/error state.
- Never block the chart on it.

**Scope and surfaces**
- Read-only: no trading changes.
- Check the mobile layout and both light and dark.
- If lib/scalable/read-tools.ts has an obvious spot, add a chat tool or artifact for "show me the chart for X".
- Disconnecting Scalable and "reset all data" must remove the stored chart data.
- Mock Scalable in tests. On the QA app, use a mocked or stand-in connection. Never call the real account.

## Rules
- Read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly. Read `gh issue view 152 --comments`.
- Branch `t3/issue-152-wealth-charts` from current `origin/main`. Commit each step in plain language, ending each message with:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Don't end your turn while a command is still running.** Wait in the same turn.
- **Never kill a process you didn't start yourself in this session, verified by PID.**
- Run one `npm ci` at a time. If it stalls, retry once with `--prefer-offline`.
- The QA app on port 3100 and the moneo-qa backend are shared with other agents:
  - Never run `npm run qa:reset` or `docker compose -p moneo-qa down`.
  - Never touch the owner's backend (.env, port 3000, project `moneo`).
  - If 3100 is busy, wait and retry.
- If you apply your migration to the shared QA database for testing, revert it afterwards, so other branches' `test:db` isn't broken.
- **Run `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` yourself and quote their last lines in your final reply.**
- Also run `npm test`, `npm run build` and `npm run test:db`.
- Use the verify-ui skill for light/dark/mobile. Link the screenshots in the PR body from a commit, then remove them from the branch.
- Push and open a PR to `main` (`Closes #152`), ending the body with:
  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
  Never merge.
- Final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.
